info.title: Fraud Investigation Transaction Lookup
info.description: Retrieve an existing synthetic PaySim transaction by its stable identifier. The response contains pre-transaction facts and source provenance. It does not determine whether fraud occurred.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key for the Fraud Investigation lookup service. Enter the key only in the Copilot Studio connection, never in this specification.

get.summary: Get an existing transaction by ID
get.description: Retrieve pre-transaction facts and source provenance for one transaction. Use this tool only when the user provides a transaction ID. A missing transaction is reported as not found; a returned transaction is not proof of fraud.

parameters.name: transaction_id
parameters.description: Stable transaction identifier: exactly 32 hexadecimal characters.

200.description: The transaction was found. Monetary values are exact decimal strings; balances are values before this transaction.

400.description: The transaction ID is not exactly 32 hexadecimal characters.

401.description: The API key is missing or incorrect.

404.description: No transaction exists for this valid ID.

503.description: The local application database is unavailable.

Transaction.description: Pre-transaction facts and traceable source information. Fraud labels and post-transaction balances are excluded.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the source CSV, encoded as 64 hexadecimal characters.

source_line_number.description: Physical line number in the source CSV. It does not establish event order within a step.

step.description: PaySim simulated time step. Transactions within the same step have no reliable ordering.

amount.description: Original exact decimal amount as a string, without a currency assumption.

oldbalance_org.description: Source account balance before the transaction, as an exact decimal string.

oldbalance_dest.description: Destination account balance before the transaction, as an exact decimal string.

Error.description: A lookup or authentication error without internal implementation details.
